author: Spec Researcher

relevant_findings.finding: Standalone decorative architectural elements (beams, columns, mantels) share identical substrate handling, material systems, and fine finish workflow with other millwork items. They differ from coffered ceiling beams (which are integrated into the ceiling grid system and handled by SF_WOOD_CEILING_NC) and from stair newel posts (handled by SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC). These are focal points -- prominently visible, often the aesthetic centerpiece of a room.

Decorative beams in NC are typically: (1) hollow box beams -- MDF or FJP shell over framing, 3 exposed faces (bottom + 2 sides), (2) solid wood beams -- reclaimed or engineered timber for rustic aesthetic, 3-4 exposed faces, (3) polyurethane faux beams -- lightweight, pre-finished or paintable. MDF and FJP are the most common paint-grade substrates. Beam profiles range from simple flat-faced box (4-6 inch faces) to large timber (10+ inch faces) to ornate carved/detailed profiles.

Decorative columns in NC are typically: (1) square/rectangular wraps -- MDF or FJP panels over structural post, 4 flat faces, (2) round columns -- turned wood, fiberglass, or PVC with paint-grade finish, (3) fluted columns -- routed detail adding significant surface complexity. Columns run floor-to-ceiling or partial-height (half-column on wall). Column capitals and bases may have ornate detail requiring slower brush work. Height modifier always applies -- top of column requires ladder/scaffold.

Fireplace mantels in NC range from: (1) simple floating shelf -- single MDF or wood piece mounted above firebox, (2) standard surround -- shelf + legs/pilasters framing the firebox opening, (3) full assembly -- elaborate surround with crown molding, dentil detail, paneled legs, possibly extending floor-to-ceiling. Substrates are typically MDF (most common in NC), poplar, or hardwood for premium installations. Mantel-to-wall caulk joint is critical. Stone/brick/tile surround is NOT in painting scope -- it is a masking target.

MDF edges MUST be sealed with solvent-based sealer (shellac-based) BEFORE latex face primer application. This prevents fiber raise and edge swelling. This is NON-NEGOTIABLE per established pipeline precedent (SF_WAINSCOT_PANEL_NC, SF_WOOD_WALL_NC, SF_WOOD_CEILING_NC). MDF architectural elements have many edges -- beam miters, column panel joints, mantel shelf edges.
relevant_findings.source: Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine SS4.1 (Primer Selection Matrix), pipeline precedent

relevant_findings.finding: Beams are overhead work -- similar to wood ceiling painting with reduced ergonomic efficiency. Production rates for beam painting should incorporate overhead factor (~0.85x of equivalent trim rates for ceiling-mounted beams). Columns require elevated work at the top -- height modifier applies per PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND. Mantels are standard wall-height work (H1 typical) with no overhead penalty.
relevant_findings.notes: Overhead factor for beams is less severe than full ceiling work (0.70-0.80x) because beams are discrete elements with accessible faces, not continuous overhead surfaces.

relevant_findings.topic: Spray vs brush for architectural elements
relevant_findings.finding: Spray is preferred for production speed and uniform finish on architectural elements. Brush is viable and sometimes necessary: (1) occupied spaces where spray containment is impractical, (2) mantels near stone/brick where masking is complex, (3) small scope (single beam or mantel). For brush application on these millwork surfaces, waterborne alkyd (BM Advance, SW Emerald Urethane) is preferred for longer open time. Roll and Tip methodology applies to flat column faces and mantel shelves.
relevant_findings.source: Fine_Finish_Doctrine SS15 (Brush and Roll Application), SS15.1.1 (When appropriate)

relevant_findings.topic: Caulk joint density by element type
relevant_findings.finding: Architectural elements have significant caulk joint requirements: (1) Beams -- beam-to-ceiling junction along full length, beam-to-wall at end supports, miter joints at beam intersections. (2) Columns -- column-to-ceiling junction (perimeter of top), column-to-floor junction (perimeter of base), column-to-wall junction (back edge if wall-mounted). (3) Mantels -- mantel-to-wall junction (all contact edges), shelf-to-leg joints, leg-to-wall junctions. Caulk work is a significant portion of prep labor on these elements.

condition_drivers.effect: SS_BARE requires full primer coat with substrate-specific chemistry (MDF edge seal + latex build, FJP stain-block, hardwood tannin-block). SS_PRIMED_FACTORY skips primer -- lighter prep only.

Controls inspection scrutiny, sanding discipline, and additional process steps. QT2 prohibited -- prominent millwork. QT3=standard. QT4=premium (full sand, systematic inspection at 3 ft). QT5=superior (thorough sand, critical lighted inspection, 3+ coats brush).
Drives protection zone activation (spray needs more protection) and production rates (spray faster). Method is configuration, not quality.
Drives beam-specific complexity modifier: small_box=1.0x, standard_box=1.10x, large_timber=1.20x, ornate=1.40x. Only applies to ITM_ARCH_BEAM.
condition_drivers.source: Adapted from Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine SS7.2 complexity categories

condition_drivers.effect: Drives column-specific complexity modifier: square_smooth=1.0x, square_detailed=1.15x, round_smooth=1.10x, round_fluted=1.30x. Only applies to ITM_ARCH_COLUMN.
Drives mantel-specific complexity modifier: shelf_only=1.0x, standard_surround=1.25x, full_assembly=1.50x. Only applies to ITM_ARCH_MANTEL.

quality_differences.QT3: Fill obvious fastener holes, caulk visible gaps, light scuff sand 120 grit for adhesion.
quality_differences.QT4: Fill all visible holes, caulk all joints thoroughly, full sand 180-220 grit.
quality_differences.QT5: Fill every hole no matter how small, perfect tooled caulk, thorough sand 220+ grit with uniform scratch pattern.

quality_differences.QT3: Quick glance inspection. Address obvious dust nibs, missed holes.
quality_differences.QT4: Systematic scan at 3 feet. Identify dust nibs, texture inconsistency, mark for attention.
quality_differences.QT5: Lighted critical inspection at arm's length. Zero tolerance for any visible imperfection.

quality_differences.QT3: Spot sand only -- visible nibs, rough spots.
quality_differences.QT4: Light full sand 220 grit. Entire surface scuffed for adhesion, all marked defects addressed.
quality_differences.QT5: Thorough full sand 220-320 grit. Uniformly smooth to touch. All defects addressed.

quality_differences.QT3: Quick visual from normal viewing distance.
quality_differences.QT4: Thorough inspection at 3 feet with raking light on beam/column faces.
quality_differences.QT5: Critical inspection at arm's length. Zero tolerance. Angled light on all faces.

failure_modes.cause: Water-based primer applied to MDF edges without prior solvent seal
failure_modes.prevention: Shellac edge seal as step 1 of two-step prime. NON-NEGOTIABLE.

failure_modes.cause: Standard primer used instead of stain-blocking primer on finger-joint pine
failure_modes.prevention: Use stain-blocking primer (shellac-based or high-quality latex stain-block) on FJP substrates.

failure_modes.failure: Caulk joint failure at beam-ceiling junction
failure_modes.cause: Insufficient caulk application or using rigid filler at a joint that experiences seasonal movement
failure_modes.prevention: Use flexible painter's caulk at all element-to-structure junctions. Allow proper cure before painting.

failure_modes.cause: Over-application of paint on vertical surfaces, particularly with waterborne alkyds
failure_modes.prevention: Thin coats on vertical surfaces. Lay flat surfaces horizontal when possible. Monitor for sags 15-20 minutes after application.

failure_modes.failure: Overspray on adjacent finished surfaces (stone surround, ceiling, walls)
failure_modes.cause: Inadequate masking when spraying architectural elements
failure_modes.prevention: Proper masking at all element-to-adjacent-surface junctions. Use masking film + tape. Check masking seal before spraying.

failure_modes.failure: Build-up in inside corners of beam/column/mantel detail
failure_modes.cause: Excessive spray pass overlap or brush overloading in recessed profiles
failure_modes.prevention: Light spray passes on detail areas. Brush out excess in corners while wet. Start with recessed detail, then flat surfaces.

notes_for_materials_manager: Same QT-driven finish systems as other millwork: SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC (QT3), SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE (QT4), SYS_FF_PREMIUM (QT5). All reuse existing SYS_ IDs.
Primer selection is substrate-driven per Millwork Doctrine SS4: MDF edges need shellac seal, FJP needs stain-block, hardwood may need tannin-block, softwood gets standard primer.
Caulk consumption higher per item than typical trim -- architectural elements have larger junction perimeters (beam-to-ceiling, column-to-floor/ceiling, mantel-to-wall).
Masking materials for spray: masking film/paper for wall/ceiling/floor protection near discrete elements. Less masking than room-spanning specs (ceiling, wall) because elements are localized.
Consumable sizing: brush 2-2.5 inch angled sash for detail work, small foam roller for flat column faces and mantel shelf (Roll and Tip method per FFD SS15.6).
Material systems are QT-driven RECOMMENDATIONS -- contractor retains discretion per RC-005.
notes_for_sop_librarian: Context prefix: ARCH -- all task IDs use TSK_ARCH_*, module IDs use MOD_ARCH_*.

Three paintable items with element-specific tasks: beam tasks (overhead positioning), column tasks (full-height work), mantel tasks (wall-height work). Shared modules for prep, prime, interstage, cleanup.
MDF edge seal is a separate task (TSK_ARCH_SEAL_MDF_EDGES) that runs BEFORE latex primer -- two-step prime sequence. Conditional on substrate_state = SS_BARE AND substrate contains MDF.
Caulk tasks should be element-specific: TSK_ARCH_CAULK_BEAM_JUNCTIONS, TSK_ARCH_CAULK_COLUMN_JUNCTIONS, TSK_ARCH_CAULK_MANTEL_JUNCTIONS -- different junction geometry and density.
Protection setup/teardown is localized (floor_workzone for spray, floor_perimeter for brush) -- not full-room like ceiling or wall specs.
Interstage process runs between every coat except final -- same pattern as all Fine Finish specs.
Height modifier applies to beam and column tasks via PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND. Mantel tasks typically H1.
Round config patterns: ROUND_ARCH_2FINISH (factory-primed, 2 finish coats), ROUND_ARCH_PRIME_2FINISH (bare, primer + 2 finish), ROUND_ARCH_3FINISH (QT5 brush, 3 finish coats).
notes_for_estimation_engineer: Three separate production rate sets needed -- one per paintable item (beam LF, column EA, mantel EA).
Beam rates: similar to trim LF rates with overhead factor ~0.85x for ceiling-mounted beams. Spray ~130-170 LF/hr, brush ~50-70 LF/hr at QT3 standard_box baseline.
Column rates: EA-based. Spray ~4-6 EA/hr, brush ~2-3 EA/hr at QT3 square_smooth (standard 8ft column). Height modifier stacks on top.
Mantel rates: EA-based. Spray ~2-3 EA/hr, brush ~1-2 EA/hr at QT3 standard_surround.
Element-specific complexity modifiers: beam_profile (1.0x-1.40x), column_type (1.0x-1.30x), mantel_type (1.0x-1.50x). These apply ONLY to their respective items.
Height modifiers from Modifier_Registry: H1=1.0x, H2=1.30x, H3=1.50x, H4=2.00x. Apply to beam and column tasks. Mantel typically H1.
QT modifiers: QT3=1.0x, QT4=1.30x, QT5=1.50x per Modifier_Registry.
Prep tasks (fill, caulk, sand) rate varies by element complexity -- ornate beam profiles and full mantel assemblies have significantly more prep than simple box beams or shelf mantels.
These are research guidance rates. Final calibration by Estimation Engineer.

proposed_new_keys.description: Running LF of standalone decorative beams (not coffered ceiling grid beams). Profile complexity handled by beam_profile modifier.
proposed_new_keys.justification: No existing key covers standalone beam painting. Beams are LF items measured by running length.

proposed_new_keys.description: Count of decorative column wraps to be painted. Size and profile complexity handled by column_type modifier.
proposed_new_keys.justification: No existing key covers column wrap painting. Columns are counted individually.

proposed_new_keys.description: Count of fireplace mantels/surrounds to be painted. Assembly complexity handled by mantel_type modifier.
proposed_new_keys.justification: No existing key covers mantel/surround painting. Mantels are counted individually.

adjacency_notes: Beams are primarily adjacent to ceiling_field (along full length) and wall_field (at end supports). Beam enamel vs ceiling flat/eggshell = different_finish typically.
Columns are adjacent to ceiling_field (top), floor (bottom, not painted), and optionally wall_field (back edge if wall-mounted). Full height means column-ceiling junction is at room height.
Mantels are adjacent to wall_field (all around) and fireplace surround (stone/brick/tile -- not_in_scope, masking target only).
Surface IDs from vocabulary: beam_wrap, column_wrap, mantel. All verified in Surface_Vocabulary_Reference.

zones.notes: Drop cloth runners near work area. Standard for brush millwork. Architectural elements are discrete -- not room-spanning.
Localized floor coverage around spray target. floor_workzone is appropriate because elements are discrete items, not room-spanning surfaces. Not full room floor_full.
Wall masking near spray target. Beam-wall junction, column-wall junction, mantel-wall junction. Masking film + tape.
Ceiling fixtures near beam spray work. Conditional on spray method and fixture proximity to beam.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Beam meets drywall ceiling along full beam length. Different finish -- beam enamel (satin/semi-gloss) vs ceiling flat. Caulk joint at junction.
Beam meets wall at end supports. Different finish -- beam enamel vs wall latex.
Column top meets ceiling. Caulk joint at perimeter of column top.
Column meets wall at back (wall-mounted columns). Freestanding columns have no wall adjacency.
Mantel meets wall at all contact edges. Different finish -- mantel enamel vs wall latex.

affected_conditions.notes: Floor protection excluded when floor is subfloor. NC may have subfloor during architectural element painting.
Rare in NC. Additional protection when occupied.
Temperature affects dry times and open time for waterborne products.
Beams at ceiling height require ladder/scaffold. Columns require ladder for top work. Height modifier applied via PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND.
MDF edge sealing uses solvent-based products -- adequate ventilation required.

valid_input_states.rationale: NC context. Architectural elements arrive either bare (custom mill work, site-built) or factory-primed (prefab decorative elements). Combined prime+paint spec handles both.

output_state.rationale: Output state varies by sheen configuration. Satin is default.

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: Protect finished ceiling from beam/column spray overspray. Unfinished ceiling needs no protection.
Protect finished walls from element spray overspray. Unfinished walls need no protection.

assumptions.source: Research extrapolation from SF_WOOD_CEILING_NC (0.70-0.80x for full ceiling)
assumptions.note: Beams are discrete overhead elements, not continuous ceiling surfaces. Overhead penalty is less than full ceiling work but more than wall-height work.

assumptions.value: 4-6 EA/hr spray, 2-3 EA/hr brush at QT3 for standard 8ft square_smooth column
assumptions.source: Research extrapolation from trim LF rates and column surface area estimation
assumptions.note: No doctrine covers column-specific production rates. These are estimates based on equivalent trim SF per column.

assumptions.value: 2-3 EA/hr spray, 1-2 EA/hr brush at QT3 for standard_surround
assumptions.note: No doctrine covers mantel-specific production rates. Highly variable by assembly complexity.

uncertainties.description: Polyurethane faux beams may require special primer (bonding primer) due to non-porous substrate. Not all faux beams are paintable. This spec assumes paint-grade architectural elements.
uncertainties.impact: Low -- most NC architectural elements are MDF, FJP, or solid wood. Poly faux beams are a niche case.
uncertainties.recommendation: Note in spec that polyurethane substrates may require bonding primer. Do not add as a separate config dimension.

uncertainties.description: Full assembly mantels vary enormously in complexity -- from simple pilaster surrounds to floor-to-ceiling overmantel with crown, dentil, and paneling. The 1.50x modifier for full_assembly may not capture the most complex installations.
uncertainties.impact: Medium -- very complex mantels may need hourly billing.
uncertainties.recommendation: Flag in production.json that full_assembly mantels exceeding typical scope should be assessed individually.
